P2_fcy_account.question: Can resident individuals hold a foreign-currency account locally?
P2_fcy_account.answer: Restricted on paper (exchange controls). Under the Exchange Control Act, anyone in Saint Lucia entitled to sell foreign currency must offer it for sale to an authorised dealer unless the Director of Finance and Planning consents to retention and use; a consent tied to a stated purpose lapses when that purpose ends (Revised Laws of Saint Lucia 2023, s.4). How banks apply this to resident USD accounts in practice was not captured: ask your bank whether you need, or it holds, consent before you keep foreign earnings in a USD account. Free-zone businesses may hold accounts in any currency (Free Zone Act, search summary).

L2_tax_id.answer: Official TIN description supplied by Saint Lucia to the OECD: "The TIN is a numeric code which is issued to individuals, and entities upon application. W1_workarounds.question: Simple, legal routes around payment barriers for a beginner (no misrepresentation, nominees or sanctions evasion)
W1_workarounds.answer: Barriers: Stripe does not accept merchants here; platforms that pay out through PayPal Payouts cannot pay PayPal accounts here (not on PayPal's Payouts list, see P4 for ordinary PayPal receiving); Wise does not let residents hold money. Simple legal routes: (1) Sell digital products or software through a merchant of record: Paddle (software/SaaS only; each seller reviewed), Lemon Squeezy (bank payouts), Polar, Dodo Payments. The platform is the legal seller to your customers, handles card payments and consumer VAT/sales tax, and pays you out. You still declare the payouts as your income at home (see L3). (2) Sell services on Upwork, which is available here (not on its restricted list). Which withdrawal methods you get (bank, PayPal, Payoneer, etc.) depends on the country and shows in your account. (3) Paid apps and in-app sales through Google Play (merchant registration available here). (4) For direct clients, a bank transfer (SWIFT) into your own local account always works. Follow the local foreign-exchange rules (see P1) and keep invoices. (5) Local official channel: By law, foreign currency must be offered to an authorised dealer unless the Director of Finance consents to you keeping it. Ask your bank whether you need consent before holding earnings in a USD account (Exchange Control Act s.4) (P2). Avoid: opening accounts with a foreign address, a relative's or friend's identity, or a VPN to look like you are elsewhere. It breaches platform terms (accounts and funds get frozen) and can break anti-money-laundering or sanctions law.
